what: SPX close candle scan, step 2 (HOLDOUT 2021-01-01 .. 2026-10-20), run on the frozen candidate list after its SHA-256 matched.
summary_plain_english: Question: does any candle near the close predict the SPX move into the close? 41 candle features were scored on 2013-2020 only; 3 reached |t| >= 2.5 and were frozen (with their direction, hashed) before any 2021-2026 bar was read. In 2021-2026, 2 of them pass the pre-registered test (one-sided, Holm 5%), i.e. 'predict' the direction better than chance, and 1 of those is 'accurate' (hit-rate CI lower bound above the option break-even).

F2_1m_1550_strong_body: 2013-2020 right 54.1%; 2021-2026 right 57.5% (95% CI 53.6%-61.2%) on 644 trades with a non-zero move (644 trades in all), mean 1.05 bps/day, Holm p 6.28e-05 -> PASSES. Option break-even 49.5% (size-neutral 51.8%): accurate. It is the known P3 effect in another form, so its holdout pass is nominal, not a blind confirmation.

F1_1m_15:50: 2013-2020 right 52.2%; 2021-2026 right 54.0% (95% CI 51.4%-56.6%) on 1444 trades with a non-zero move (1445 trades in all), mean 0.92 bps/day, Holm p 0.0109 -> PASSES. Option break-even 51.5% (size-neutral 51.9%): NOT accurate enough to pay for the option. It is the known P3 effect in another form, so its holdout pass is nominal, not a blind confirmation.

F4_day_so_far: 2013-2020 right 52.0%; 2021-2026 right 48.4% (95% CI 45.8%-51.0%) on 1446 trades with a non-zero move (1446 trades in all), mean -0.03 bps/day, Holm p 0.526 -> fails. Option break-even 51.0% (size-neutral 51.6%): NOT accurate enough to pay for the option. It is the known P1 effect in another form, so its holdout pass is nominal, not a blind confirmation.

F2_1m_1550_strong_body economics (pre-registered model: buy the ATM 0DTE option at the entry, cost = half the realized-move-fair straddle + $0.10 + $0.09): mean option P&L +46.1 $ per trade, t 2.22 (iid) / 2.06 (NW). The CI lower bound 53.6% clears both the primary break-even 49.5% and the size-neutral 51.8%; the primary one is below 50% only because moves on right days were 1.046x the average in 2021-2026. Fragile: the verdict flips if the market charges more than 1.085x the realized-fair straddle, and the mean P&L is 0 at 1.166x. Measured on 22 Robinhood days: straddle / its own payoff = 0.90 (95% CI 0.62-1.38), too few days to tell which side of the tipping point the market is on.

F2_1m_1550_strong_body over time (descriptive): 2021-2022 right 63.0% of 216 trades, NW t 3.56, option P&L +80.7 $/trade (t 2.33); 2023-2026 right 54.7% of 428 (CI 49.9%-59.3%: includes 50%, includes the size-neutral break-even, just clears the primary one), option P&L +28.6 $/trade (t 1.11, not significant). Most of the holdout edge comes from 2021-2022.

F2_1m_1550_strong_body, trades needed to confirm going forward (5% one-sided, 80% power, about 112 trades a year): option P&L 808 trades (~7.2 years) if the full 2021-2026 effect is the truth, 2165 (~19.3 years) at the 2023-2026 effect; hit rate vs the size-neutral break-even 483 (~4.3 years); vs the primary break-even 244 (~2.2 years, assumes the bigger moves on right days persist).
F1_1m_15:50 passes the holdout test but is not accurate: its CI lower bound 51.4% is below its break-even 51.5%.

Placebo (same candles at 11:51 with the target to 11:59, 2021-2026): F2_1m_1550_strong_body t 0.61; F1_1m_15:50 t -1.09; F4_day_so_far t 0.48. Nothing there, as expected if the effect is specific to the close.

Target caveat: the test uses the Dukascopy CFD to the 15:59 bar close; the option pays on the official SPX settlement. On 22 overlapping days their 15:51 -> close moves agree in sign on 86% of days. If the disagreements are unrelated to the signal, the hit rate against the settlement would be about: F2_1m_1550_strong_body 55.4% (CI lower 52.6%).

Chance check on the real data: with the 41 signals shifted against the real 2013-2020 targets (304 shifts), on average 0.34 features reach |t| >= 2.5 by chance, 1.0% of shifts give 3 or more, and 0.0% give a best |t| of 3.82 or more.

Plain answer: 2 feature(s) pass the holdout test and 1 is 'accurate': F2_1m_1550_strong_body, which is the already-known P3 effect (the 15:50 one-minute candle), so this is a nominal pass, not a new or blind discovery. It clears the accuracy bar only just: under the exact fair-straddle cost assumption, on the CFD series rather than the settlement, and mostly because of 2021-2022. Treat it as a lead to forward-test, not an established edge. The other 39 features are not shown to predict: 38 never reached the discovery bar and 1 candidate(s) failed the holdout. The pre-registered forward test (descriptive) has not been run: 1 day of data.

decisions_and_interpretations.text: Each feature is assigned the earliest pre-registered entry its candles allow: a feature whose candles all close by 15:48:59 uses entry 15:49 (target r(15:49 open -> 15:59 close)); a feature that uses the 15:49 or 15:50 one-minute bar uses entry 15:51 (target r(15:51 open -> 15:59 close)). So F1 15:30..15:48 and F3 15:20..15:40 enter at 15:49; F1 15:49, F1 15:50, every F2 shape (the 15:50 1-minute candle and the 15:45-15:49 five-minute candle, which closes at 15:49:59) and F3 15:45 enter at 15:51; every F4 feature is a 'day level at entry' and enters at 15:49.
decisions_and_interpretations.kind: implementation choice (the pre-registration's entry rule applied feature by feature)

decisions_and_interpretations.text: F4: P = open of the entry bar (15:49). CLV = (P - day low)/(day high - day low) with high/low over the 1-minute bars 09:30..15:48 and P itself; signal sign(CLV - 0.5), 0 if high = low. Opening gap = sign(09:30 open - prior session's 15:59 close). Prior-day candle = sign(prior session's 15:59 close - its 09:30 open). The prior session is the previous NYSE session in d1_days.csv (calendar != nyse_holiday); if that session is not in the keep set (no bars) the two prior-day features are undefined for that day (dropped, not zero). Day-so-far = P1 = sign(ln(15:49 open / 09:30 open)).

F2 candle = (open of its first minute, max high, min low, close of its last minute); body = close - open, range = high - low, upper wick = high - max(open, close), lower wick = min(open, close) - low. strong body: sign(body) if range > 0 and |body| >= 0.6 range, else 0. hammer: +1 if range > 0, lower wick >= 2|body| and lower wick >= 0.6 range, else 0. shooting star: -1 if range > 0, upper wick >= 2|body| and upper wick >= 0.6 range, else 0. engulfing vs the prior candle of the same size (1-minute 15:49; five-minute 15:40-15:44): +1 if prior close < prior open, current close > current open, current open <= prior close and current close >= prior open; -1 for the mirror case; else 0. big candle: sign(body) if |body| >= 2 x the median (high - low) of the day's 1-minute bars from 09:30 through the candle's last minute, else 0. A candle with any of its bars missing is undefined (dropped).

The P3 reference row is P3 exactly as in spx_close_1549/analysis.py: sign(ln(15:51 open / 15:50 open)), entry 15:51. It is never eligible as a candidate and is outside the BH family. F1 15:50 (sign(close - open) of the 15:50 bar) and the F2 shapes on the 15:50 candle are in the 41 as the pre-registration lists them; any candidate whose non-zero signals agree with P3 on >= 90% of discovery days is flagged overlaps_known_P3, because P3's 2013-2026 result (which includes the holdout years) was known when the pre-registration was written, so its holdout is not a clean out-of-sample test.

Per feature: y = signal x target x 1e4 over days where both are defined; mean and Newey-West t (lag 5) over all those days (zero-signal days contribute 0, as in analysis.py); hit rate = share of days with signal != 0 and target != 0 on which signal x target > 0. Discovery p-values are two-sided normal; BH q-values over the 41. Holdout: one-sided normal p of mean > 0 with the frozen direction; Holm over the candidates. Hit-rate 95% CI = Wilson score interval treating days as independent.
decisions_and_interpretations.kind: implementation choice (statistics as in analysis.py where it has them)

decisions_and_interpretations.text: Buy one ATM 0DTE call (signal x direction > 0) or put (< 0) at the entry price, strike = entry price (idealised ATM), hold to the 15:59 close. Payoff = |move| on correct days, 0 on wrong days (a zero move counts as wrong). Option cost = half the realized-move-fair straddle = 0.5 x mean |move| over the candidate's holdout trade days, + $0.10 half-spread + one fee ($0.09 or $0.74 per contract = 0.0009 or 0.0074 points; no exit fee at expiry, as analysis.py). Break-even hit rate = cost / mean |move| on correct days (primary, uses the correct- vs wrong-day |move| distribution); also reported: the size-neutral break-even cost / mean |move| (= 0.5 + (spread + fee)/mean|move|) and both at the last D1 price level (moves in return units x the 2026-10-20 15:49 open). Trades needed (one-sided 5%, 80% power, iid normal approximation): n = ((z_a + z_b) sd / mean)^2 for the per-trade signed return and for the per-trade option P&L; for the hit rate vs 50% and vs the break-even, n = ((z_a sqrt(p0 q0) + z_b sqrt(p q)) / (p - p0))^2.
decisions_and_interpretations.kind: implementation choice (the pre-registration's step 4 made concrete)

decisions_and_interpretations.text: Cross-check: on the 22 Robinhood 10-minute days the ATM straddle = call + put 15:40-bar close (last trade in 15:40:00-15:49:59, about 15:50) at the strike nearest the SPX 15:49-bar close, in bps of that SPX price, versus the assumed realized-move-fair straddle (D1 holdout mean |move| in bps, for the 15:49 and 15:51 entries, which bracket a 15:50 mark) and versus the official |settle - S| on the same days. The two fully priced days use the 15:49 one-minute marks: 2026-10-20 from spx_close_1549/results.json, 2026-10-21 from the live scorecard (settlement provisional there).

Placebo: every candidate rebuilt 240 minutes earlier (every bar index - 240: entry 15:49 -> 11:49, 15:51 -> 11:51, target to the 11:59 close; F1 15:40 -> 11:40, etc.), with its frozen direction. Opening gap and prior-day candle keep their signal (only the target moves); day-so-far becomes sign(11:49 open / 09:30 open). Reported on discovery and holdout, descriptive.

The holdout step was re-run on the same frozen file (hash unchanged) after its first run, to change two reporting items: (a) the straddle-cost sensitivity had scaled the option cost by market straddle / D1 holdout mean |move|, a ratio across different volatility regimes (2026 vs 2021-2026) that made the break-even look far too low (about 36%); it now uses the market's markup over the realized official move on the same 22 days, with a bootstrap CI; (b) the plain summary now states the P3 overlap, the 2023-2026 descriptive hit rate, the size-neutral break-even and the calendar time to confirm. No test statistic, candidate, direction, or pre-registered economics number changed (the code is deterministic).
decisions_and_interpretations.kind: DEVIATION in reporting only (labelled), made after seeing the first holdout output

decisions_and_interpretations.text: The pre-registration says the hit rate excludes (and counts) zero signals. The primary hit rate here also drops trades whose target move is exactly 0, as analysis.py does; those trades are counted (n_trades_zero_target). Because the option economics treats a zero move as a paid trade with zero payoff, every hit rate is also reported with zero-move trades counted as misses (hit_rate_zero_target_as_miss and its Wilson CI), and the accuracy verdict is given under both.
decisions_and_interpretations.kind: DEVIATION (minor, disclosed by the audits): extra exclusion in the primary hit rate; the economics-consistent version is reported next to it

decisions_and_interpretations.text: After the two audits (audits/DISPOSITION.md) the holdout step was re-run on the same frozen file, and the discovery step was re-run first (same candidates and directions, frozen file kept byte for byte, hash unchanged). Added, all reporting: (a) the direct one-sided test of the option P&L per trade (iid and NW t) and the straddle markups at which the break-even reaches the hit-rate CI lower bound and at which the mean P&L is 0; (b) the accuracy verdict against the size-neutral break-even and trades needed against it; (c) holdout sub-periods 2021-2022, 2023-2026 and each year, with each period's own economics and trades needed at its effect size; (d) the straddle cross-check against the straddle's own payoff |settle - K| next to |settle - S|, the same-day payoff for the two fully priced days, and the markup sensitivity on both; (e) the D1 CFD target vs the official SPX settlement target on the overlapping Robinhood days, and the hit rate mapped to the settlement; (f) known-effect flags for P1 as well as P3 (computed in the holdout step; the frozen file is unchanged); (g) a real-data null check (random-sign signals and circular shifts of the real signals against the real D1 targets); (h) the provenance changes in the module docstring. Nothing in the pre-registered steps 1-4 changed: no feature, candidate, direction, test, threshold or pre-registered economics number.

robinhood_10m_days.how_to_read: ratio_market_to_own_payoff_same_days (added after the audits) is the like-for-like markup: the straddle is struck at K, so its payoff is |settle - K|. ratio_market_to_realized_same_days divides by |settle - S| instead (S = the SPX 15:49 close; |K - S| <= 2.5 points). 1 = priced at realized-move-fair, the pre-registered assumption. Either way this is an approximate cross-check on 22 days, not a validated pricing multiplier. The ratio_market_to_assumed_fair_* values compare these 2026 days with the D1 holdout average, i.e. different volatility regimes: below 1 they say the recent move is smaller than the 2021-2026 average, not that options are cheap.
robinhood_10m_days.note: 10-minute closes are last trades in 15:40:00-15:49:59 (about 15:50), not simultaneous with each other or with SPX; the straddle (call + put) is much less sensitive to that than either leg

fully_priced_days.ratio_note: ratio_market_to_assumed_fair_* compare one 2026 straddle with the 2021-2026 (or 2023-2026) average move: a volatility-regime comparison, not a pricing check. Use the same-day straddle vs its own payoff instead.
